rv.q: Stroman delivers surprise after surprise, intertwining expertly executed pratfalls with choreographic virtuosity...there’s not a moment here that doesn’t delight. Who could ask for anything more? Perfection.
Right now, with the world seemingly going to hell in a handcart, it’s a care-banishing elixir; one which might just restore your faith in humanity too.
Everything in this show is joyous
Stroman's choreography for I Got Rhythm is a freely improvised, show-stopping company hoedown, re-purposing corrugated iron and pickaxes, and throwing in some tap routines on tin pans.
This delicious confection of a musical banishes the cares of the world with sublime songs and dynamic tap routines.
It’s escapist nonsense. And it bowled me over.
It is obviously fun, a veritable themepark ride of a show.
A... thing musicals can do is leave you awed by the performers’ skill. Crazy for You, a cobbled-together Gershwin comedy, throws classics such as I Got Rhythm and Shall We Dance? into the mix.
The whole evening is full of joy.
Susan Stroman's Crazy For You is pure musical theatre heaven.

Song and dance man Charlie Stemp stomps and stamps his mark on yet another all-singing, all-dancing feel good musical, this time CRAZY FOR YOU which has just opened at the Theatre and is nothing short of Stemptastic. Crazy For You at the Theatre. Charlie Stemp and cast.
This current iteration is very much the best of them all.
With irresistible performances and inspired staging, this has the potential to send London a little crazy this summer.

‘Crazy For You’ is the kind of show that should be used as an example of what the perfect musical looks like. This feel good family fun, crowd-pleasing show will guarantee you have a smile on your face all through the show… and long after you leave the theatre.
Susan Stroman's direction and choreography are breathtaking and the cast is equal to her demands.
Crazy For You is a rare treat, it’s a sumptuous, feel-good extravaganza, that could be enjoyed over and over again.

cn.t: Critics rave about this "dazzling" and "glorious" revival, hailing Susan Stroman's spectacular choreography and Charlie Stemp's sensational lead performance. The Gershwin-scored production is deemed "pure musical theatre heaven" and a "gold-standard" spectacle.
